clue.text: One who considers ditching husband for potter

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away, so the husband's letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a thinker is one who considers things

explanation.surface: A pensive person abandons their husband and runs off with a pottery maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' looks like a maker of pots, but here it is the verb: to potter about aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter and to tinker both mean to fiddle about idly with small jobs, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Blunt possibly in raising flatbread expertise

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: roti is an Indian flatbread
art means skill, expertise

explanation.surface: A baking note about the skill of making flatbread rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Blunt was the art historian exposed as a Soviet spy; 'Blunt' looks like an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt is an example of one who betrayed his country, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Pearl having bit of Edna cremated

indicators.note: a bit of the words is taken, the letters lying across them

explanation.surface: A pearl keeps a little of Edna's ashes after her cremation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the lustrous substance of which pearls are made.

clue.text: Choose surveyors for wiring

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RICS is the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, the UK surveyors' professional body

explanation.surface: Picking surveyors to inspect a building's wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: The electrics of a house are its electrical system, the wiring and fittings.

clue.text: Take sixty seconds before introduction to George Smiley

parts.note: 'be a min' is informal for taking a minute, sixty seconds

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: A spy-thriller moment: pausing a minute before meeting George Smiley, le Carré's spymaster.
explanation.walkthrough: George Smiley is John le Carré's spy, which makes 'Smiley' look like part of a name; it is the definition, read as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beaming wears a broad grin, so they are smiley in the sense of cheerful-faced.

clue.text: Mole maybe from Flanders to swap France with Belgium

indicators.note: swapping one thing with another means a letter is exchanged in the word

parts.note: Flemish describes something from Flanders
F is the international vehicle code for France
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A spy from Flanders trading his French cover for a Belgian one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests a spy; it is a skin mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole on the skin is one example of a spot or mark that spoils the surface.

clue.text: Shave second off test … that's easily enough

indicators.note: shaving takes a little off, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a sample is something taken for a test

explanation.surface: Shaving a second off a trial run proves easily good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than sufficient.

clue.text: Nordic tailor in red lace

indicators.note: to tailor is to cut and alter, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian tailor dressed in red lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor' reads as a noun; it is the anagram verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a native of Iceland, one of the Nordic nations.

clue.text: Bad smells overlooked by good people

indicators.note: in a down clue being overlooked means having something above, so G goes on top

parts.note: reeks are bad smells

explanation.surface: Good people tactfully ignore bad smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' suggests ignored; it means sat beneath in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks are a people, the nation of Greece.

clue.text: Mineral adhesive fixing agent recalled

indicators.note: fixing means holding in place, so the adhesive grips the other letters

parts.note: gum is an adhesive

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A sticky substance used to fix things, with an agent called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns round only the agent, SPY, not the whole assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is a soft calcium sulphate mineral used to make plaster.

clue.text: Example of revolutionary artist with a revolutionary print

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
type is printed lettering, print

explanation.surface: An art-world note about a rebel painter and a radical print.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'revolutionary' does two jobs: first a reversal signal on RA, then a definition of CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the model or classic instance of something, a prime example.

clue.text: Capsule of cyanide on food portion

indicators.note: in this across clue, 'on' means placed after the food

parts.note: a pie is a kind of food

indicators.note: a capsule encloses its contents, so the word's outer shell, first and last letters, is taken

explanation.surface: A spy's cyanide pill hidden on a plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capsule of cyanide' suggests the suicide pill; it is the outer letters C and E of 'cyanide'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or a slice of something, as in a piece of cake.

clue.text: Message heads to the West encrypted and in Latin

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters, so the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: et is the Latin for 'and'

explanation.surface: A coded dispatch sent westward, written partly in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short message posted on the social network formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: Small bundle holds diamonds: rector finds storage in kitchen

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the bundle wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a pack is a bundle
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A clergyman discovers a little parcel of jewels stashed away.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice rack is a shelf unit for keeping jars of spices, kitchen storage.

clue.text: Mass of endless queries shocked maiden

indicators.note: shocked suggests jolted into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
without its end, so the last letter of the word is cut

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman is shaken by never-ending questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter, leaving QUERIE, which 'shocked' rearranges into REQUIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A requiem is a Mass said or sung for the souls of the dead.

clue.text: Predicaments in annual assembly covered by paper

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside, so the assembly goes within

parts.note: quires are sets of sheets of paper
an AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: Awkward situations at a company's annual meeting reported in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' suggests a newspaper; it is quires, sheets of writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Quagmires are boggy ground, figuratively difficult situations to get out of.

clue.text: Compound in Hungary ideal for torture

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

indicators.note: torturing twists something out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim suggestion that Hungary is the perfect place for torture.
explanation.definitionFit: A halide is a chemical compound of a halogen such as chlorine with another element.

clue.text: Rogue state also maybe in deep water

indicators.note: a rogue state behaves erratically, suggesting the letters run wild

explanation.surface: A rogue nation also finds itself in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue state' reads as a phrase; 'Rogue' is the anagram signal. 'maybe' marks the definition as a figurative example.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lost at sea, literally or figuratively, means being adrift and out of one's depth.

clue.text: Capital idiot wears new gold

indicators.note: wearing puts the idiot in clothes, so the idiot sits within the other letters

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an ass is a fool, an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool shows off by dressing in brand-new gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Acceptable number still regularly used vessel

parts.note: U means upper-class, acceptable
ten is a number

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A reasonable quantity of still regularly used vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or container, including a vessel used in cooking.

clue.text: Warrant finally delivered here prior to court action

indicators.note: prior to means coming first, so these letters precede the rest
finally points to the last letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: a serve is an action on a tennis court

explanation.surface: A legal warrant is delivered here before proceedings in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court action' suggests a lawsuit; it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to merit or be entitled to it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Instruction from Berlin? Fool around on army time

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to kid is to fool
TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: An order from Berlin to mess about on army time.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed by authority; the word is German, hence Berlin.

clue.text: Final recipient of unstable uranium needs recipe

indicators.note: unstable suggests the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A nuclear chain: unstable uranium needs a recipe to reach its destination.
explanation.definitionFit: An end user is the person who ultimately uses a product, the final recipient.

clue.text: Song put soldier on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places one piece above the other

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A song that puts a soldier on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' suggests a person; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a song of praise or allegiance, such as a national anthem.

clue.text: Mention North American approaching East European by radio

indicators.note: heard over the airwaves, so the word is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A North American nears an Eastern European contact over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American' looks like one unit but splits into N and AM; 'approaching' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A namecheck is a mention of someone by name, especially in public acknowledgement.

clue.text: Tree-climbing included in tradecraft

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing goes upward, so the letters read backwards
included in means the letters lie within the word

explanation.surface: Tree-climbing as part of a spy's training.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is a large coniferous tree.

clue.text: Bug concealed after aide-de-camp deserted

indicators.note: after means the concealed piece follows the other letters
deserted means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A military aide abandons his post and goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' suggests desertion from the army; it empties 'aide-de-camp' to its outer letters A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect, a bug in the everyday sense.

clue.text: Pilgrim fooled. Journey's beginning on island

parts.note: to be had is to be fooled, tricked

indicators.note: the beginning is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pilgrim tricked at the start of a journey to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A hadji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca.

clue.text: Extremely huge stick can be a ruler

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A huge stick could serve as a ruler for measuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick; it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod the Great was a king of Judea, a ruler in the Bible.

clue.text: Defect of feet, back and flanks

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: paws are animal feet
flanks are sides

explanation.surface: An anatomical defect affecting the feet, back and sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defect' looks like a noun for a flaw; it is the verb, to change allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to change allegiance, crossing to the other camp.

clue.text: Wind and spray both sides crossing midpoint of dam

parts.note: a spray of fine droplets is a mist

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the two sides hold the middle letter between them

parts.note: right and left, R and L, are both sides

indicators.note: midpoint means the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wind whips up spray on both banks across the middle of a dam.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold northerly wind blowing through southern France.

clue.text: A classic Russian luxury vehicle skirts Italian road

indicators.note: skirts means goes round the edges, so the vehicle encloses the road

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
via is Italian for road

explanation.surface: A grand car drives around an Italian road in Russian style.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is sturgeon roe, a delicacy strongly associated with Russia.
